Dances run on select Fridays from 7 to 10 with a live band and a caller, and every dance is taught, so no partner or experience is needed. Get there at 6:45 for the beginner lesson, and bring clean soft soled shoes and a water bottle. It costs $12, $5 for ages 12 to 18 or anyone on a limited budget, and nothing at all under 12. The hall moves between Burlington and Shelburne, so check the schedule before you head out.

notes.queen-city-contras: Every dance taught, no partner needed, a beginner lesson before the band

95.source: Ride a ferry across the lake to New York
95.title: Ride a ferry across the lake to New York
95.paragraph: Lake Champlain Ferries has been crossing this lake since 1826, and walking on is the best cheap boat ride around, $5.50 each way for an adult or $12.25 with your car, before any fuel surcharge. Head to the Charlotte dock at 2901 Ferry Road, where it's about 25 minutes and 3 miles across to Essex, New York, with the Adirondacks and the Green Mountains on either side. Up north, the Grand Isle to Plattsburgh crossing runs 24 hours a day, year round, in about 14 minutes. There are no reservations, so just show up 15 minutes early.

notes.lake-champlain-ferries: Walk on for $5.50, and the Grand Isle crossing runs 24 hours, year round

96.source: Swing an ice axe up a frozen waterfall
96.title: Swing an ice axe up a frozen waterfall
96.paragraph: Petra Cliffs, the Burlington climbing gym, takes beginners outside from December through March for a one day Intro to Ice Climbing, in groups of one to six. Guides certified by the AMGA teach crampon and ice axe technique on frozen waterfalls, and they bring the harness, helmet, ropes and the rest of the technical gear. Your part is warm layers, food, water and your own ride to the ice. Book a date, and your guide will send the exact meeting spot ahead of time, usually the parking lot for that day's climb.

notes.petra-cliffs: Burlington's climbing gym runs one day beginner ice courses, December to March

97.source: Eat your way through the Champlain Valley Fair
97.title: Eat your way through the Champlain Valley Fair
97.paragraph: Come for a weeknight after work or a full weekend day at the Champlain Valley Expo in Essex Junction, and bring cash for the $10 parking. Start with the barns and the free shows, which in 2026 meant sheep shearing in the Livestock Barn, a daily parade and a BMX stunt show, then let the kids milk a cow at Old McDonald's Farm. Eat your way across the grounds, ride the midway once the sun goes down, and catch a free grandstand show with your admission. Buy tickets only through Etix, the fair's official seller, and skip the resellers.

notes.champlain-valley-fair: Vermont's largest annual event, ten days at the Expo in Essex Junction

98.source: Run or cheer the Vermont City Marathon
98.title: Run or cheer the Vermont City Marathon
98.paragraph: If you're running, sign up early, since early bird pricing through December 31, 2026 puts a 2 person relay at $185 and a 3 to 5 person team at $240, and a relay is the friendliest way in for folks who'd never run a full marathon alone. If you're cheering, plant yourself on the Church Street Marketplace or along the bike path, where marathoners come by twice on the new two loop course, and listen for the Taiko drummers. Then walk down to Waterfront Park for the finish, which now comes downhill past Union Station through a row of trees.

notes.vermont-city-marathon: Vermont's biggest one day sporting event, with relays for 2 or 3 to 5

99.source: Throw a round of disc golf
99.title: Throw a round of disc golf
99.paragraph: Borrow a driver, a midrange and a putter from the South Burlington Public Library, which lends disc sets for up to 2 weeks, and head to Awasiwi Woods behind Munsen Field. The 9 basket course winds through the trees, with grey tees for a short round and blue tees for a tougher one, and it's open dawn to dusk. After school hours, park at the middle school and walk across the fields. Once you're hooked, drive up to Smugglers' Notch Resort for Brewster Ridge, a wooded, technical course ranked #6 in the world by UDisc, or the Village 9, playable in 30 minutes to an hour.

notes.awasiwi-woods-disc-golf: South Burlington's own 9 basket woods course, open dawn to dusk
notes.smuggs-disc-golf: Brewster Ridge and Fox Run Meadows, ranked #6 and #8 by UDisc

100.source: Make a bakery run beyond downtown
100.title: Make a bakery run beyond downtown
100.paragraph: Start in South Burlington at Mirabelles, 3060 Williston Road, and look for the creme brulee cake, the best seller, chiffon layered with vanilla custard. Head out Route 15 to Poorhouse Pies in Underhill, where more than 60 kinds of pie are baked daily and the pocket pies go fast, so come early. Another day, drive to Middlesex for Red Hen Baking, which now does all its baking there and sells its most popular breads and pastries at a self serve Bread Box stand from 8 to 5 every day, or until it sells out. Look for the Miche or the Kingdom Rye.

notes.mirabelles-bakery: South Burlington cake case, best known for its creme brulee cake
notes.poorhouse-pies: Over 60 pies baked daily in Underhill, plus pocket pies that sell out
notes.red-hen-baking: Vermont bread since 1999, now baked in Middlesex with a self serve stand

101.source: Stop at a real Vermont general store
101.title: Stop at a real Vermont general store
101.paragraph: Start at the Jericho Center Country Store, Vermont's longest running store, with breakfast from the counter and a wander through the shelves of a business that has been open since 1807. Then drive down to Charlotte for coffee or lunch at the Old Brick Store on Ferry Road, a general store with 170 years behind it that now pours espresso and natural wine, and skip Tuesday, when it's closed. Finish at the Shelburne Country Store on Falls Road with a slab of its own fudge and a bag of penny candy before it closes at 5.

notes.jericho-center-country-store: Vermont's longest running store, open since 1807
notes.old-brick-store: A 170-year-old Charlotte store turned café, wine and staples shop
notes.shelburne-country-store: House-made fudge and penny candy in a building from about 1835

102.source: Walk or bike the Stowe Recreation Path
102.title: Walk or bike the Stowe Recreation Path
102.paragraph: Park at Lintilhac Park behind the Stowe Community Church in the village and start up the Stowe Recreation Path, crossing back and forth over the West Branch of Little River with the mountains ahead of you. It's 5.3 paved miles to the Topnotch end on the Mountain Road, so turn around wherever your legs tell you to. Some of the path was paid for by townspeople buying pieces of it at $2 an inch. In winter, come back with snowshoes or cross country skis, since the town keeps it open all year.

notes.stowe-recreation-path: A 5.3 mile paved greenway along the West Branch, open all year
